title: Geometric Lemma For Diagonal Reduction
body_html:
Geometric Lemma For Diagonal Reduction

Let $\beta$ be a semisimple element of depth $r$, and let

$$ \mathfrak g^\dagger_{x,-t} $$

denote the diagonal part of $\mathfrak g_{x,-t}$ with respect to the brick decomposition. The current theta draft states that for each $-t<r$,

$$ G_{x,r-t}\bigl(\beta+\mathfrak g^\dagger_{x,-t}\bigr) = \beta+\mathfrak g_{x,-t}. $$

In particular, for $s=r/2$,

$$ G_{x,s}\bigl(\beta+\mathfrak g^\dagger_{x,-s}\bigr) = \beta+\mathfrak g_{x,-s}. $$

This lemma is used to replace the condition

$$ M(w)\in\beta+\mathfrak g_{x,-s} $$

by the stronger diagonal condition

$$ M(w)\in\beta+\mathfrak g^\dagger_{x,-s} $$

after acting by $G_{x,s}$.

Draft Caution

The current TeX states this lemma but does not prove it. The existing spec contains a proof sketch based on surjectivity of $\operatorname{ad}(\beta)$ on off-diagonal associated graded pieces.
